items.title: GOP rep: 'We got to investigate' Starlink slowdown report
items.summary: Republican Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick is calling for a congressional investigation into reports that SpaceX CEO Elon Musk personally ordered a Starlink slowdown in Ukraine, with Democrats also demanding an investigation. The alleged decision to reduce satellite speed and access has life-or-death consequences for Ukraine's military operations. Musk and the Trump administration have given conflicting accounts of whether the slowdown occurred.

items.title: Supreme Court won’t revive Trump administration’s transgender inmate policy; Thomas, Alito dissent
items.summary: The Supreme Court refused the Trump administration's request to stop providing hormone treatments and surgeries to transgender inmates, declining to lift a lower court's block. Justices Thomas and Alito dissented from the decision. The Bureau of Prisons policy would have tapered treatments for affected inmates.

items.title: Pennsylvania warns doctors about rising rates of rare congenital measles
items.summary: Pennsylvania's health department issued a warning to doctors about rising measles cases during pregnancy and increasing congenital measles infections—a disease rarely seen in the U.S. Congenital measles occurs when a newborn contracts measles infection from a pregnant mother.

items.title: Zelensky says he'd be open to freezing front lines to end Russia war
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would be open to freezing the front line to end the war with Russia while preserving much of Ukraine's territory. He stated, 'Right now, we have to freeze, and I think this is a real way to end this war.'

items.title: DOJ, judge clash over Trump's East Potomac Golf Course takeover
items.summary: Trust is breaking down between the Department of Justice and the judge overseeing President Trump's bid to take over East Potomac Golf Course, a public golf course in Washington, D.C. The tensions highlight judicial skepticism toward the administration's project.

items.title: Putin orders release of jailed American as he meets Trump envoy for Ukraine talks

items.title: Woman told Russell Brand he treated her ‘like an animal,’ court hears

cards.title: Start with tiny wins, not resolutions
cards.insight: Major behavior change fails when people attempt large transformations overnight. Small, consistent actions build momentum and create psychological reinforcement that sustains long-term shifts.
cards.takeaway: Pick one small habit (5 minutes daily) instead of overhauling your routine; build from there over weeks.

cards.title: Stack new habits onto existing ones
cards.insight: Attaching desired behaviors to established routines eliminates the need to create willpower from scratch. Your brain treats the anchor habit as a trigger, making the new behavior automatic over time.
cards.takeaway: Pair your new habit with something you already do daily—after coffee, before bed, or during commute.

cards.title: Track visible progress, not just effort
cards.insight: Humans are motivated by measurable evidence of change. Seeing a visual record of consistency—even small wins—activates reward pathways that reinforce behavior, making continuation feel natural rather than forced.
cards.takeaway: Use a calendar or app to mark days completed; review weekly to see tangible progress accumulating.

cards.title: Design your environment, not just your willpower
cards.insight: Behavior change is easier when friction is removed from desired actions and added to undesired ones. People follow the path of least resistance; altering your surroundings is often more effective than relying on discipline alone.
cards.takeaway: Remove temptations from sight and place reminders or tools for your desired habit where you'll naturally encounter them.
